title: A local linear fit gives a positive depth and post-transit flux slope for K2-22 in 108 K2 Campaign 1 orbits
abstract: We test whether the flux excess after transit increases with core depth in K2-22. In K2 Campaign 1, a local linear baseline and fixed windows give a noise-corrected slope of 0.0647 in 108 orbits. The conditional 95 percent block interval is 0.0216 to 0.1185. A quadratic baseline and a wider core window give intervals that include zero. An early fit gives a later prediction gain of 6.0 percent, with an interval from -1.3 to 11.6 percent. A small-aperture difference depends on a few orbits. EVEREST gives a positive slope but shares K2 exposures. Of 7273 independent ground-photometry rows, only two distinct epochs pass the same coverage rules. They cannot confirm the relation. Synthetic tests recover slopes under the assumed white-noise model. A fixed optically thin dust cloud is consistent with the main result, but its physical cause remains unconfirmed. We report no new planet or source. Code, compact inputs, exact raw hashes, controls, figures and offline instructions are included.
